entities.summary:
Gaspare Ricciullo del Fosso, O.M. (1496–1592) was a Roman Catholic prelate who served as Archbishop of Reggio Calabria (1560–1592), Bishop of Calvi Risorta (1551–1560), and Bishop of Scala (1548–1551).


Del Fosso played a crucial role in the Counter-Reformation, collaborating closely with Pope Pius IV (1547–1559) to reform the Catholic Church in Italy. His efforts led to the establishment of the Congregation for the Reform of the Church, a key institution in the Catholic Church's efforts to combat Protestantism.


As Archbishop of Reggio Calabria, Del Fosso oversaw the construction of several major churches and monasteries, including the Basilica of Reggio Calabria, a prominent pilgrimage site.


Del Fosso's legacy extends beyond his ecclesiastical career, as he was also a patron of the arts, supporting local artists and writers.


Despite his significant contributions to the Catholic Church, Del Fosso's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery, with few records of his family or personal relationships available.


In the end, Del Fosso's dedication to his faith and his people led to a lasting impact on the Catholic Church in Italy, cementing his place as a key figure in the Counter-Reformation.
